scenario_summary: Customer is seeking a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which falls outside the standard 30-day refund window policy.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Lakisha Jackson and I'm 38. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Lakisha, thank you for reaching out. I understand how frustrating it is to return from travel and find an unexpected charge. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your subscription?
Sure, my account number is 8849201 and the email is l.jackson@email.com.
Thank you for that information. For security, could you please confirm the last four digits of the payment method on file and the date the cancellation was processed in our system?
The card ends in 4492, and I canceled it on the 10th of last month.

I have verified your account details, thank you. I see the cancellation request was indeed processed 34 days ago. While our 'Service Refund Policy 4.2' strictly limits automated refunds to 30 days post-cancellation, I can see you have been a loyal customer for three years with no prior refund requests. Because you reached out promptly upon your return, I am authorized to make a one-time exception for your account.
Oh, that would be amazing! Thank you so much for understanding.

You are very welcome, Lakisha. I have processed the refund for the full amount of $49.99 back to your card ending in 4492. You should see that reflected in your bank statement within 3-5 business days. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account and, noting the customer's long-term loyalty and prompt contact, applied a one-time policy exception to issue a full refund despite the request being 4 days past the 30-day window.

judge_scores.justification: The agent handled the out-of-policy refund request with exemplary verification and empathy, validating account details appropriately without being overly burdensome. Furthermore, the agent took direct concrete action within their authority by citing specific policy rules while granting a well-reasoned one-time exception based on customer loyalty.
